title: US-supplied HIMARS launchers begin to change Ukrainian strike capability
body:
The M142 High Mobility Artillery Rocket System (HIMARS) entered Ukrainian service in June 2022. According to a Washington Post report published on 24 July 2022, the first of what became a dozen launchers arrived that month, after which the United States announced four more, bringing the total to 16. Britain and Germany each sent or pledged three similar systems.

Ukrainian forces used the launchers against Russian command posts, ammunition depots and logistics hubs. One strike hit an ammunition depot in Izium. In the Kherson region, strikes targeted the Antonivskyi Bridge, a key Russian supply route across the Dnipro. Dmytruk, a battalion commander in Ukraine's 93rd Mechanized Brigade, told the newspaper that Russian shelling against his unit fell to about one tenth of its earlier level after a HIMARS strike on a nearby depot, and that concussion casualties dropped from two or three a day to about one a week.

Ukrainian officials described the system as important. Defence Minister Oleksii Reznikov said at least 100 HIMARS would be needed for an effective counteroffensive and called the weapon a game changer. Military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov said Ukraine had not lost a single launcher. Russian Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu was reported to have ordered commanders to make HIMARS a priority target, and Moscow claimed to have destroyed at least four systems, a claim Ukraine denied.
